title: 2026-01-18-precision-pathologies-kv-affinity-and-coldstart-hunt
summary: Deep technical review digging into a recent accuracy regression after moving to AWQ/INT8 hybrid, experiments showing KV cache affinity causing stale prefixes under sticky routing, and a proposed hunt plan for cold-start-induced noise with targeted benchmarks and canary rollout steps.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-18 09:30 UTC — duration ~62m; recording from Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Maya (Orchid ML), Tom (Orchid SRE), Priya (Orchid Platform)
[00:00] Lena: okay starting, thanks everyone for jumping on; quick agenda review — regression context, what we saw in prod, profiling artifacts, and a hunt plan.
[00:22] Maya: cool thanks. so last week we rolled the AWQ integer pipeline and noticed a 3.6% drop in our abstractive summarization rouge-l on the nightly job, and also some tail latency spikes at cold start.
[00:45] Carlos: when you say AWQ pipeline — is that full-awq across all layers or layerwise?
[00:52] Maya: it's hybrid — GPTQ for embeddings, AWQ applied to transformer layers 1-18, int8 on the dense output. we did a layerwise sweep but the canary used the full profile.
[01:12] Tom: latency spikes were mostly after autoscaler events or node restarts, so cold starts. P95 went from 220ms to 410ms for first few requests in a session, then warmed.
[01:28] Carlos: got it. two hypoth — accuracy noise from AWQ quantization sensitivity, and second, KV cache affinity causing staleness where warm KV isn't reused after routing changes.
[01:44] Priya: also note our VPC setup uses a NAT gateway with occasional connection churn — could amplify cold-starts.
[02:01] Lena: good. quick check, do you have the canary's exact commit and quant config?
[02:10] Maya: yes, canary id abc123, quant-config: awq-8-per-channel, int8-output-per-tensor, no stochastic-rounding. I can drop the config link in the notes.
[02:27] Carlos: thanks. oof okay so first, accuracy: AWQ tends to introduce structural bias when exponent ranges shift — we saw that earlier on long-form generation, but typically GPTQ behaves differently because it preserves weight distributions more. Are you seeing hallucination increase or just metric drop?
[02:48] Maya: mainly decreased ROUGE and some examples with truncated completions — like the model ends sentences abruptly more often. Examples included in the gist.
[03:05] Tom: on the infra side, KV cache miss rate jumps after an instance is replaced — even though session affinity is supposed to be sticky, our LB occasionally routes to a different pod during autoscale. That leads to recompute and longer tail latencies.
[03:26] Carlos: that routing switch could also change effective prompt prefix alignment — cold KV populates different key indexing due to sharding differences. if the KV cache warm-up diverges you'll see both latency and potential content drift.
[03:44] Maya: interesting. we also saw divergence when batch sizes were reduced from 8 to 2 under low qps — perhaps batching interacts with quantized kernels.
[04:02] Carlos: yes batching + INT8/AWQ kernels can change numerical ordering and accumulation rounding; small batches may trigger different fused-kernel paths.
[04:20] Lena: okay let's get empirical. propose we split the investigation into three parallel tracks: 1) precision sensitivity sweep (layer-drop & per-layer quant check), 2) KV affinity and routing reproducibility tests (sticky vs random), 3) cold-start microbench + batching kernel path profiling.
[04:41] Priya: sounds good. question though — how intrusive are the layer sweeps? we prefer to avoid long canaries if possible.
[04:50] Carlos: we can do offline evals on your dev dataset first and run microbench on a single on-prem node. then small canaries with a 5% traffic weight.
[05:05] Maya: do we have tooling to bisect which layer causes most delta? we had a layerwise script but it's heavy.
[05:13] Carlos: we use a 'layer-swap' harness — quantize all but one layer back to FP16, iterate. I'll share the script, it runs fairly quick if you parallelize on multiple CPUs.
[05:26] Maya: perfect. also curious about AWQ's interaction with KV cache lifetime; could quantization change tokenization boundaries or token IDs?
[05:36] Carlos: not token IDs per se, but quantization affects logits scaling, which can shift top-k decisions, and that upstream change can alter subsequent KV keys used, causing divergent cache entries. so small numeric shifts can cascade.
[05:53] Tom: okay so it's plausible the two issues compound — AWQ introduces small semantic shifts, and routing/cache churn magnifies those in prod.
[06:05] Lena: what about fallback strategies? we have model-variant fallback — send to FP16 for low-confidence outputs or when kv-miss rate high?
[06:14] Carlos: yes Redwood runtime supports runtime fallback by confidence thresholds and also by latency SLO breaches. We can configure a policy: if cold-start detected or kv-miss ratio > X, route to FP16 model variant. But that doubles cost for those requests.
[06:30] Priya: cost's okay for a short window, but we need to quantify how often it would trigger. Tom, can you surface autoscale churn logs for last week?
[06:38] Tom: yep will attach.
[06:41] Maya: also, do we have any signal from evals about which prompts are most sensitive? maybe certain templates break more.
[06:49] Carlos: we should run your failset through AWQ vs FP16 and compute per-prompt delta; Redwood Optimize can produce a sensitivity heatmap. I'll run a job.
[06:59] Lena: action items — let's list them after we finish. continue.
[07:06] Carlos: a few technical notes: AWQ uses blockwise quant with per-channel scales and compresses range; it tends to be more biased for outlier rows. GPTQ preserves more tails but also uses more storage. INT8-per-tensor output layers can introduce saturation on projection layers which hurts repeated attention heads.
[07:32] Maya: that matches our error examples — repeated noun phrase collapse in long outputs.
[07:40] Tom: about the KV cache: we identified a hotspot where the cache index serialization changed between releases — small endian vs big-endian mismatch in our custom sharding code; not Redwood's runtime but our middleware. could that amplify divergence?
[07:59] Carlos: for sure — mismatched key encoding will produce misses. even minor encoding drift results in cold recompute and divergence because new cache entries won't line up with previously cached prefixes.
[08:12] Priya: ack, we'll patch and test.
[08:18] Maya: any risk that AWQ causes non-deterministic outputs due to quantization rounding? we've seen some non-determinism tied to fused kernels and different BLAS libs.
[08:31] Carlos: yes, fused kernels + parallel reduction order can be non-deterministic across run-to-run, especially with mixed-precision. Determinism options exist but sometimes cripple perf. We can enable deterministic kernels on canary only.
[08:47] Lena: okay let's look at concrete experiments and timeline. Carlos?
[08:52] Carlos: propose these experiments (est. wall clock):
- E1: Offline layer-swap sweep on canonical eval (runs 3h, parallelizable)
- E2: Kernel-path profiling with batch sizes {1,2,4,8} on an on-prem node — capture kernel path logs and per-layer numerical diffs (1.5h)
- E3: KV routing reproducibility test — replay traffic against sticky vs random LB routing with same model and measure key hit/miss & output divergence (2h)
- E4: Small canary 5% traffic with runtime fallback enabled and deterministic kernel toggle (24-48h monitor)
[09:36] Maya: ok estimates fine. which of these require Redwood infra changes?
[09:41] Carlos: E2/E4 touch runtime flags (deterministic kernels, fallback thresholds), E3 is mostly traffic replay so minimal. E1 is offline. I can produce patches and a short runbook.
[09:53] Priya: for E4 we need to pre-approve cost and an SLA clause for canary rollback — legal will need a note.
[10:02] Lena: we can do an accelerated rollback policy — automated rollback if rouge delta > 1.5% or error rate up by 1%.
[10:12] Tom: sounds good.
[10:14] Maya: quick question about metrics — should we weight per-prompt importance by product traffic? some rare prompts are noisy but not important.
[10:22] Carlos: yes weight by traffic and also track an importance score from your production telemetry. Redwood Optimize can ingest that.
[10:30] Priya: one more infra note: our VPC egress to Redwood control plane has occasional 2s spikes due to packet inspection; could that present as cold-start in our logs if signals to warm cache are delayed?
[10:42] Carlos: potentially, yes. it's a network-induced cold-start effect. We should correlate control-plane comms with warm-up events.
[10:49] Lena: good call.
[10:52] Maya: ok let's surface a tentative timeline — E1/E2/E3 within 72h, E4 after results, target to have canary within a week.
[11:02] Carlos: I can start E1 and E2 today if you grant a dev node access.
[11:08] Priya: I will provision two nodes and share creds.
[11:12] Lena: perfect. any competitor tools mentioned?
[11:16] Tom: we briefly looked at another vendor's runtime but didn't do deep evaluation; names were 'CloudInferenceX' and 'FastServeAI'.
[11:25] Carlos: ok noted.
[11:27] Maya: quick clarifying question: is AWQ reversible? if we decide to roll back it's straightforward to re-deploy FP16 variant?
[11:35] Carlos: yes it's just model variant swap in the runtime, might take a few minutes to route traffic; for long-running sessions we may still get warm/cold effects but new requests will hit FP16.
[11:45] Priya: we want a plan for observability — can we get per-request markers for quant-path used, kv-hit boolean, and kernel-id?
[11:54] Carlos: yes Redwood Console can emit per-route traces with those attributes; I'll enable a debug trace stream for the canary.
[12:02] Maya: great.
[12:05] Lena: quick recap and next steps.
[12:08] — RECAP —
[12:08] Lena: 1) Carlos to run layer-swap and kernel profiling and share scripts/logs (E1/E2)
[12:15] Carlos: will do, deliverable: results gist + sensitivity heatmap.
[12:19] Lena: 2) Tom/Priya to provision dev nodes and share logs from LB/autoscaler churn.
[12:24] Tom: will attach last 7 days of autoscale events and NAT/gateway logs.
[12:28] Lena: 3) Maya to share failing prompt set and canary commit id (she already did) and tag important prompts.
[12:35] Maya: will add importance scores.
[12:38] Lena: 4) Redwood to propose fallback policy config and canary rollback thresholds.
[12:44] Carlos: propose: fallback when kv-miss ratio > 20% or first-request latency > 350ms for more than 5% of requests; rollback if aggregated ROUGE drop > 1.5% across weighted set.
[12:59] Priya: accept in principle, will confirm with legal.
[13:03] Lena: final Qs?
[13:06] Maya: none, thanks.
[13:08] Lena: thanks all, will follow up with notes and a runbook.
[13:12] (call ends)
next_steps: Carlos to run layer-swap sweep and post sensitivity heatmap
Tom to attach autoscaler and NAT gateway logs for last 7 days
Maya to tag failing prompt set with importance and share exact canary commit
Redwood to prepare fallback policy and canary runbook for approval

Tom Reynolds: provide autoscale/NAT logs by 2026-01-19
